messages:
incident-bot: PAGER (P1) — Elevated 5xx rate detected on api-gateway (edge -> gateway). Region: eu-west-1. Trigger: 2m error rate > 6%. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/stream. Alert TS: 3210004567. Paging on-call SRE.

jordan.sre: Ack — I'm on pager. Jumping into logs now. @kei-api can you join for routing/backends?

kei-api: On call. Checking gateway pools + LB. Any customer-facing reports?

sam-support: Got two customer tickets reporting 502s in last 6m (TICKET-12345, TICKET-12346). Both mention timeouts and partial responses. No big churn yet but multiple retries.

ava-cs: Holding on comms until we know blast radius. I'll draft a short message to affected customers once we confirm mitigation.

ops-bot: Recent changes: deployment gateway-v2.3.1 rolled at ~3210004300 to 8/10 nodes. Autoscaler events: none in last 10m. No infra maintenance scheduled.

jordan.sre: Collecting pod logs — tailing last 5m for gateway proxies:
```
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=gateway -c proxy --since=5m | grep -E "(502|504|upstream reset)" | head -n 50
# sample: 502 upstream read timeout from upstream=10.2.4.18:8080; request_id=x-req-9f2a
```

jordan.sre: Counts show ~900 5xx in 5m across gateways, spike started ~3210004400. Many show backend connection reset / upstream timeout.

kei-api: Checking upstream health — model-serving pool shows transient increased latency around same window. Querying envoy stats: 
```
curl -s http://gateway-metrics.local/metrics | grep 5xx | tail -n 20
# metrics show 502s concentrated on route /v1/generate from envoy-cluster model-backend-v1
```

maya-frontend: I can repro in browser with sample request, getting 502 with id x-req-9f2a. Full client stacktrace shows socket timeout ~12000ms then 502.

jordan.sre: Hypothesis: upstream model-backend instances are saturating / hitting transient TCP resets causing proxy to return 502/504. Two mitigations to try in parallel: 1) divert traffic away from suspect backend pool; 2) increase gateway capacity + reduce concurrent connections per upstream via RPS throttling.

kei-api: Initiating quick traffic shift to fallback pool (model-backend-v2) at 20% to validate:
```
# trafficctl is internal routing tool
trafficctl set-weight model-backend-v2 20 --route /v1/generate
```

ops-bot: trafficctl change accepted, change id tc-98765. No rollout errors.

jordan.sre: Meanwhile bumping gateway replica targets to absorb burst:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/gateway --replicas=20
```

kei-api: Also toggling envoy retry config on route to add 1 retry with per-try timeout 3s to avoid long client waits. Pushing change now.

jordan.sre: Observability update: 30s after traffic shift + scale, 5xx rate dropped from ~6.5% -> ~1.4%. Latency tail also improved.

sam-support: Customer tickets updated: two customers reported errors are subsiding. I'll add note that we're mitigating and monitoring.

ava-cs: Sending high-level update to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated 502/504 errors affecting some requests. Mitigation in progress; more updates shortly."

kei-api: Deciding next steps: keep fallback weight at 20% for 10m, monitor for regressions. If stable, perform progressive 50% shift and then full cutover. Also need postmortem to determine root cause in model-backend capacity.

jordan.sre: Agree. I'll keep watch for 30m, then hand off to oncall rotation in 25m for longer-term follow-up. Please capture any correlated deploys or infra events.

ops-bot: Note: No node autoscaler events, but three gateway pods OOM-killed ~3210004380-3210004420 on one node (node-az3). Investigating node pressure.

kei-api: OOMs could explain backend instability if co-located services starved. I'll check model-backend pod metrics for memory spike.

jordan.sre: Action items captured: [A] Keep fallback at 20% and monitor (owner: kei-api). [B] Maintain scaled gateway replicas for 30m (owner: jordan.sre). [C] Check node memory pressure / eviction root cause (owner: ops-bot). [D] Customer comms (owner: ava-cs). Add to incident board.

sam-support: Thx — pushing update to customer tickets now.

maya-frontend: I'll add a temporary client-side retry guidance for tenants that implement exponential backoff to reduce hammering during the spike.

jordan.sre: Current status — mitigation effective, error rate reduced to ~1.1%. We'll keep channel open for 45m. If anything regresses call pager again. :thumbsup:

kei-api: I'll leave fallback in place and collect heap/disk metrics from model-backend for postmortem. Planning a rollback of gateway-v2.3.1 if we see more OOMs correlated with that rollout.

ops-bot: Logged events and snapshots to incident archive id inc-3210004567.cron.

jordan.sre: Handoff in 25m to @kei-api for follow-up. If stable after 45m we can close the pager and start a postmortem. Final note: no broader customer outage; impact concentrated to high-throughput routes.

ava-cs: I'll queue a follow-up comms update in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident P1 status: Mitigated -> monitoring. Please update incident channel with any new findings.

jordan.sre: Summary for postmortem stub: spike of 502/504 caused by backend connection resets and node-level memory pressure during recent gateway rollout; mitigations: traffic diversion to fallback pool, scaled gateway replicas, temporary retries, customer comms. Owners assigned.

kei-api: Adding logs/metrics links to the incident board and creating initial RCA draft.

jordan.sre: Closing active triage — switching to monitoring state. Handoff complete.
